sentence_stem: Yesterday we played football in the park, so
correct_completion: we were very tired in the evening.
full_sentence: Yesterday we played football in the park, so we were very tired in the evening.

options.why_wrong: Watching a film is not a logical result of playing football, so it does not complete the cause-effect link that 'so' introduces.
This repeats the cause from the first part of the sentence. 'So' needs a result, not the same event.

options.text: we were very tired in the evening.
we ate dinner at a restaurant.
options.why_wrong: This is a new event that does not follow from playing football, so it breaks the cause-effect logic.

grammar_focus: Past simple with 'so' to show a result
explanation: 'So' introduces a result of the first clause. After 'so', we need a past simple clause that describes what happened as a consequence of playing football.
translation: Ayer jugamos al fútbol en el parque, así que por la tarde estábamos muy cansados.
